events.credibility_reason: Known only from search snippets: author, date and status unestablished, body unread; claims the same analytic route the audit flags.

why: The statement asserts only the upper bound vol(K) <= (n+1)^n/n!; it names no equality clause. So OpenAI's all-dimension inequality is whole (the Lean signature matches the hypotheses), unreviewed (the Sienicki audit is engagement that did not complete verification, and a Lean build is not digestion), doubtful because the audit names concrete unverified analytic steps but no error, and generated by Astra per OpenAI's quoted statement. Liu's equality characterisation and Nill-Paffenholz's toric equality case answer a stronger question than the bullet asks, so variant; Liu's AI role is generated by the author's own account (Danus produced the proof from a human observation). Berman-Berndtsson 2011 is a statement about toric KE manifolds with no convex-geometry claim, so variant; their 2012 Crelle paper settles the inequality for a class of rational polytopes, a case. Ehrhart's dimension-2 and simplex cases are a pre-snapshot case. Agama's counterexample claim is set aside as not credible on several signals at once. The Anthropic-hosted PDF cannot be dated, so after_snapshot null. Alpoge's post settles nothing.
doubts: Treating the equality clause as outside the statement follows the bullet's wording; if the conjecture is read to include it, OpenAI's event becomes a case and Liu's (which depends on OpenAI's unverified analytic half) would be needed to complete it. The OpenAI AI-role quote comes from secondary coverage, not OpenAI's own page. The Sienicki audit authors' qualifications and whether the chapter reports were human-written are unestablished. The 1964 date for Ehrhart's special cases may be the date of the conjecture rather than of the proofs.
